# Affliction Warlock — what the bots run

**Recommendation (what the bots run).** Build (levels 10-60), 35/11/5 — no respec, one build from level 10 to 60. The decision loop walks 129 rules in ascending priority and executes the first whose condition is true. The party fixtures place this spec on level 38 (2 members), level 48 (2 members), level 51 (1 member), level 60 (7 members). [measured on bot runs, private 1.18.1-based realm — `knowledge/classes/warlock/affliction/talents.yaml`, `rotation.yaml`]

**Measured in round 155** (amp-6's per-spec table). **OK** — 68% of the human spec median (303 vs 445.4 boss DPS over 65 boss fights); felhunter damage invisible; DoT mix correct [measured].

**This page is the bots' half.** It records what our party bots actually run for this spec — the level-60 build and the level-by-level order, the rule firing order the decision loop walks, the kit bands, the round-155 measurement and the recorded deviations. The hand-written guide for this spec is [affliction.md](./affliction.md).

## Situational notes from the rule notes

Every sentence below is copied from a rule's own note (the rule id is in front of it) and mentions a situation the rule exists for. Rest, food and drink rules are left out here; their items are in the band table above.

- **WA00b-unending-breath — Unending Breath:** HO-TKB-PLAY-144 (round 131 BFD-C, p4-pioneer water.py: party uptime submerged 77.6%, the shaman's 18 Water Breathing casts spread 4/4/4/3/3 with 4 on a druid already in Aquatic Form while the mage was covered 35.6% of her time underwater): covered_by [131, 1066] (v30): a member in Aquatic Form or carrying the other breath buff is skipped. HO-TKB-PLAY-139 (owner, 2026-10-08: the party's shaman or warlock buffs every member before a swim and refreshes it while the party is underwater; druids use Aquatic Form for their own swims): Unending Breath (5697, instant, 10 min, 30 yd) on every member, the resident included, who lacks it or has under two minutes left (party_missing with refresh_below_ms, v28), while the party walks or holds at a swim stretch (party.swim_ahead, p4-group 343) or any member is submerged; in combat too, since a buff running out mid-fight underwater is how a member drowns.
- **WA00d-demonic-sacrifice — Demonic Sacrifice:** The guide's before-the-pull list begins there: "summon the Imp and Demonic Sacrifice it for +4% spell damage. Sacrifice the Succubus instead if you are threat-capped" (guide/classes/warlock/affliction.md L19; the effect table at L176-L180: Imp +4% spell damage, Succubus -10% threat, Felhunter mana regeneration; staff post Jamey 2025-07-25, and Soul Entrapment adds +6% with no demon out).
- **WA00t-voidstone — Use Voidstone:** The guide: "Carry a Felstone, or a Voidstone for threat" (guide/classes/warlock/affliction.md L19), "Stone: Felstone by default; Voidstone if threat is the problem" (L236), "Voidstone: -10% threat, 15% with Improved Stones" (L167: Afraido's table 90% threat with Demonic Sacrifice (Succubus) or Voidstone alone, 81% with both). Above WA00t-felstone on purpose: the walk reaches Voidstone, then Felstone, and each one's `not aura_self` on the OTHER stone's aura is what stops the pair trading auras every tick.
- **WA00t-felstone — Use Felstone:** In OUR DB it is ITEM 51934, created by Create Felstone 51698 (spell_level 32, one Soul Shard), on-use spell 51697 (spell row L26505: a 30-minute dummy aura; the guide's words at L171: it returns 3% of damage dealt as healing and also heals the demon, with the same page's warning that the healing generates threat and can pull mobs onto the warlock). `not aura_self(52751)` as well as its own aura: the stones are one mutually exclusive personal buff, so the Felstone must not overwrite the Voidstone the rule above just applied for threat -- the walk reaches Voidstone first while threat is high, and this rule takes over only after that stone has expired.
- **WA01c-summon-succubus — Summon Succubus:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows with the tkb-play gate: Level 60 only: the levelling guide keeps the Voidwalker as the solo demon until 60 (leveling.md L205, L221, L244, L270); the Succubus and the Felhunter are the 60 choices of the spec page.): THE SUCCUBUS HAD NO SUMMON RULE IN ANY OF THE THREE WARLOCK FILES (spec audit 2026-10-18, sub-60 gap 3; su damage pet from level 20 is named in the guide and the pet table, and only Imp and Voidwalker were ever summoned). The Succubus does more damage but is squishy" (L205), so this rule fires only when the warlock is alone and above 70 per cent health and the walk falls through to WA01d-summon-voidwalker-solo below it when it is not -- the Voidwalker stays the safe solo pet and this is the "many players switch" branch, not a replacement.
- **WA01e-summon-felhunter — Summon Felhunter:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows with the tkb-play gate: Level 60 only: the levelling guide keeps the Voidwalker as the solo demon until 60 (leveling.md L205, L221, L244, L270); the Succubus and the Felhunter are the 60 choices of the spec page.): THE FELHUNTER HAD NO SUMMON RULE EITHER, AND THE GUIDE GIVES IT ONE JOB: mana. "Felhunter: mana regeneration" (guide/classes/warlock/affliction.md L180), "sacrifice the Imp, or the Felhunter if mana is your limit" (guide/classes/warlock/destruction.md L23, L182: "sacrifice the Felhunter instead of the Imp to Life Tap less"), and the pet table calls it the utility/PvP pet (guide/classes/warlock/demonology.md, Pets section).
- **WA01-demon-armor — Demon Armor:** HO-TKB-PLAY-013 (OQ-2568): out of combat this rule waits while the resident drinks or eats (aura 432, 433 or 435). With Bots.DrinkHoldsUnlessHurt 0 any cast stands a seated resident up, and in rounds 11-17 buffs, pet upkeep, dispels and non-emergency heals ended drinks and meals out of combat in every mana spec streamed (docs/research/tkb/play/r17-rest-breaks.txt).
- **WA01d-summon-voidwalker-solo — Summon Voidwalker:** HO-TKB-PLAY-031 (orchestrator, round-47 delta-0 split): ALONE, from level 10, the Voidwalker is the levelling pet (guide: "Voidwalker, with Torment on autocast"; "Send the Voidwalker"; "the general leveling pet"). An Imp that is alive is not replaced: the pet predicates do not say which demon it is, so the Voidwalker comes when the Imp has died or been dismissed.
- **WA01a-summon-imp — Summon Imp:** THE WARLOCK HAD NO PET AT ALL, IN ANY OF ITS THREE ROTATIONS, AND A WARLOCK WITHOUT A DEMON IS NOT A WARLOCK. The Imp is the one this rule summons and the archive decides it, not preference: "every common-demon summon except Imp costs a Soul Shard", so the Imp is the only demon a bot can re-summon without a resource the vocabulary cannot see; the Voidwalker is explicitly not an answer -- "Attempting to use the demon as a tank: Voidwalker threat does not scale and consistently loses aggro even at higher character levels" -- and a dungeon party already has a warrior tank; and the Imp is the one that does damage at range (Firebolt) and carries Blood Pact for the party, which the archive prices by naming its loss a mistake ("Letting the Imp die to AoE and losing Blood Pact").
- **WA01b-health-funnel — Health Funnel:** 004 removed its Health Funnel because its only available guard was `not aura_self(6307)`, which is FALSE exactly while the Imp is alive and hurt -- the one state in which funnelling helps -- and TRUE while there is no pet to funnel to; from priority 14 that would have spent every in-combat tick above 70 per cent health. The reason is gone: `pet.exists`, `pet.alive` and `pet.hp_pct` are state-vocabulary v3 predicates implemented in Expr.cpp, so the rule can now ask the question it always needed to ask.
- **WA00s-caster-first-10499 — Shadow Bolt:** Its spell list (tkbplay-201.result.txt: 104990, Wail of Souls 17631, 7,580-8,059 hp, level 58-60) is instant and not interruptible per p4-group (spell_template: castingTimeIndex 1, interruptFlags 0; not re-read here), so no interrupt rule can answer it and killing it is the only kit answer; same shape and gates as the 10471 rule, just ahead of it.
- **WA02-life-tap — Life Tap:** This rule carried NO combat gate, and out of combat that put it in a loop with the drink rule above it: WA00-drink is gated on `not aura_self(432)`, so once the drink aura is up the drink rule is FALSE and this rule takes the tick -- converting health to mana that the drink is already refilling for free. MEASURED on d-20260917T141056Z-pop: 293 Life Tap pushes on Corvane, 179 of them (61 per cent) OUT OF COMBAT, and 120 of those 179 with the Drink aura 432 already on the warlock; 586 CAST_START for 293 pushes.
- **WA00s-peel-11197 — Shadow Bolt:** Other Stratholme Undead adds are not sourced.
- **WA00s-caster-first-10471 — Shadow Bolt:** Mana Burn 17615 is instant and not interruptible (CastingTimeIndex 1, interruptFlags 0), so killing the caster is the only kit answer. amp-4's own count: the Acolyte/Neophyte pair is the killer in 149 of 263 deaths, but only 3 of 42 windows were kill-order-limited, so this is the orchestrator's ask, not the largest lever.
- **WA00s-caster-first-10470 — Shadow Bolt:** Mana Burn 17615 is instant and not interruptible (CastingTimeIndex 1, interruptFlags 0), so killing the caster is the only kit answer. amp-4's own count: the Acolyte/Neophyte pair is the killer in 149 of 263 deaths, but only 3 of 42 windows were kill-order-limited, so this is the orchestrator's ask, not the largest lever.
- **WA02a-pet-attack — pet attack:** HO-TKB-PLAY-048 (orchestrator, p4-group 123; HO-P4-GROUP-123 read round 79): send the pet at the resident's target once the fight is on, and again on a target change (pet.attacking is true only when the pet's victim is MY target). A defensive player pet ignores its owner's attack while it is out of combat (PetAI::OwnerAttacked returns when the pet is not in combat and its owner is a player), so with no rule that sends it in it fought only what hit it or its owner: on the tank's target on 84 of 169 in-combat ticks in round 79.
- **WA03-shadow-ward — Shadow Ward:** HO-TKB-PLAY-013 (OQ-2568, OQ-2569): out of combat this rule waits while the resident drinks or eats (aura 432, 433 or 435). Once the eat rule stops re-pushing into its own aura, nothing else holds a self-defensive, a form, an aura or a mana cooldown back while seated, and any cast stands the resident up (Bots.DrinkHoldsUnlessHurt 0).
- **WA03dc-death-coil — Death Coil:** HO-TKB-PLAY-117 (decision 177): the guide's emergency, "Death Coil (42) to heal and stop a mob, then Healthstone" (guide/classes/warlock/leveling.md L254): below 35 per cent with the mob on the warlock, before Fear (WA04, the same health line).
- **WA03h-howl-of-terror — Howl of Terror:** HO-TKB-PLAY-273 (leveller pass; guide leveling.md L259, L242): from level 40 the guide has the warlock Fear one mob or use Howl of Terror (2 s cast, 150 mana, 40 s cooldown, DB) when a pull goes bad (tagged vanilla baseline in the guide). The file had Fear for one mob and no Howl.
- **WA04-fear — Fear:** Gated hard: on target.attacking_self as well as health, because a feared mob runs into the rest of the room and a warlock who fears at full health has cost the party more than it saved. Fear at under 35 per cent health is a way out of a fight that is being lost; against a mob at 30 per cent or less the way out is to finish it, which a DoT tick or one more bolt does while a Fear only gives it eight seconds to come back at full strength.
- **WA04m-banish-moon — Banish:** HO-TKB-PLAY-120 (owner-approved, TortoiseBots review LEARN 1: crowd control on the party's CC mark): Banish on the Moon-marked mob when it is a demon or an elemental (`target.creature_type(3)` or `(4)`); 100 mana at rank 1, 1.5 s, 30 yd; ranks 710 and 18647. The same two branches as the mage's MF04p-polymorph-moon: a marked mob without the aura while two enemies are engaged (or one, if the mark has no victim yet), and again only under 3 s left while another enemy is engaged.
- **WA04a-curse-of-recklessness-feared — Curse of Recklessness:** HO-TKB-PLAY-024 (portfolio audit): GAP (a): "a Curse of Recklessness on the feared mob stops it fleeing, so it stays in place" (warlock/leveling.md L193, from 14, post-1.18.1; again at L317). WA04-fear is this file's defensive Fear; a feared mob running free in a dungeon pulls the next pack.
- **WA04e-curse-of-shadow-levelling — Curse of Shadow:** HO-TKB-PLAY-273 (leveller pass; guide leveling.md L249, L309; amp-4 review): from 44 the affliction curse is Curse of Shadow, and Malediction (talent, level 31 in the build) makes the same cast also afflict the target with the highest Curse of Agony rank (DB 52546), so one cast is both curses; before 44 the rank-1 Recklessness trick (WA05m) stands. Curse of Shadow is learned at 44 (rank 2 at 56), 150 mana at rank 1 (DB 17862, 17937).
- **WA05m-curse-of-recklessness-malediction — Curse of Recklessness:** HO-TKB-PLAY-122 (decision 177, vocabulary v24 rank): levels 31-43, with Malediction (the guide's Affliction table takes it at 31): "cast a rank-1 Curse of Recklessness instead: it costs 35 mana and still applies your max-rank Curse of Agony"; "Before 44, keep using rank-1 Recklessness. If Curse of Agony falls off, recast it yourself" (guide/classes/warlock/leveling.md L76, L226, L249).
- **WA05-curse-of-agony — Curse of Agony:** 25 mana, instant, 24 s of damage over time, and Improved Curse of Agony 3/3 is in this build. The spec's curse, and the reason the other curses are not here: the file takes one and keeps it up.
- **WA07-siphon-life — Siphon Life:** It is the third aura this file keeps on the target and the one that pays for the health WA02 spends.
- **WA08a-rain-of-fire — Rain of Fire:** Rain of Fire is a level-20 trainer spell in the generated warlock kit, available to every spec, and was absent from the affliction and demonology rotations entirely. THRESHOLD 4 IS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN: every one of the three warlock playbooks carries `aoe_threshold: 4`, and each puts Rain of Fire there by name -- Affliction "4+ stacked targets; Affliction has no AoE of its own", Demonology "Rain of Fire, condition: pack cleaves", Destruction "Rain of Fire, condition: melee cleave or fire-reflect makes standing in melee unsafe".
- **WA09-immolate — Immolate:** Last of the auras because it is the only one an affliction build has no talent for.
- **WA04b-fear-second — Fear:** HO-TKB-PLAY-038 (orchestrator; p1-loop v12 answers OQ-2817): Fear (5782, level 8, 15 per cent of base mana, 1.5 s, 20 yd) on the OTHER attacker, after the DoTs: this rule sits below Agony, Corruption and Immolate, so the kill target carries them first, which is the guide''s order ("DoT both, then Fear the one that is not on you", "Fear B after its DoTs are on", "Fear breaks on new spell applications, not on DoT ticks, so DoT BEFORE you Fear"). The spell has no creature-type mask; a fear-immune creature takes two casts and is then skipped for ten seconds.
- **WA13l-wand-below-34 — Shoot:** Order inside the rule: after the DoTs (50-70), Rain of Fire (85), Immolate (89), Fear (91) and ahead of Nightfall Shadow Bolt (95), Drain Life (98) and Drain Soul (100), so it repeats their guards: no Nightfall proc (aura 17941 stands and Shadow Bolt takes the tick), health at 60 per cent or more (Drain Life takes it below).
- **WA10f-drain-soul-finisher — Drain Soul:** HO-TKB-PLAY-346 (amp-5 review of HO-330, the shard budget; leveling.md L186, L282, L283): Drain Soul on a dying non-boss target, so the warlock gets Soul Shards back the way a human does (finish with Drain Soul when you need shards). Why it is needed: the Soul Shard stacks to 3 (DB item 6265) and the kit carries a stack count agreed with p4-pioneer (2 stacks, 6 shards, for destruction and affliction, 1 stack, 3, for demonology; p4-pioneer change, before the 23:00 CEST regeneration; dropped to one stack if this finisher makes the second unnecessary after a round).
- **WA08-dark-harvest — Dark Harvest:** The tree's last point and this file's fourth target aura. The guide's third guard, no interruption expected, has no term and is not written.
- **WA13w-shoot-trash — Shoot:** HO-TKB-PLAY-065 (owner approved, via the orchestrator: wand earlier on trash, keep the full spells for bosses and big pulls; the warlock ended 10 of 56 round-86 fights under 20 per cent mana): the wand instead of the filler when the target is under 30 per cent health, or the warlock is under 40 per cent mana, in a fight that is not a boss or a big pull (`not (target.ttd_ms >= 15000)`: a target that will take 15 s or more is a long fight, null reads true; `enemies_engaged_within(30) <= 3`: four or more keep the spells; `party.pull_is_boss` is true only while a pull is imminent).
- **WA12a-wand-solo — Shoot:** The guide for 4-9: "Corruption -> Immolate -> wand", from 8 "Curse of Agony -> Corruption -> wand"; and the bot-ready loop: "Nightfall proc -> Shadow Bolt. In a party nothing changes (`not (party.lowest_hp_pct >= 0)` is the solo test the rogue Stealth rule uses).
- **WA12-shadow-bolt — Shadow Bolt:** In an affliction file it is what happens when every aura above it is already up, which in a long fight is most globals and in a short one is none.
- **WA13-shoot — Shoot:** Measured on d-20260917T070130Z-p3, actor 358: the wand was 26 per cent of the mage''s casts, 86 per cent of its starts were unasked, 7 ticks were wand-locked, and 35 of its own casts came back SPELL_FAILED_INTERRUPTED -- the bot''s own movement cancelling its own auto-repeat. `not self.moving` is the other half and is the 35 interrupted casts: a wand shot the bot walks out of is a lock bought for nothing.

## What the bots do not do (from the rule notes)

Sentences from the rules' notes that say what is deliberately not implemented, or that name an open question.

- **WA03h-howl-of-terror:** The 3-mob and 50 per cent numbers are mine (proposed open question P273-2).
- **WA09-immolate:** The guide bracket lists stop naming Immolate from level 8 (L166); the L229 line gives 30 (open question P273-1).
- **WA10f-drain-soul-finisher:** Elites are left to the Dark Harvest finisher (WA08, HO-276) and the Drain Soul filler (WA10), so `not target.elite` is added here.
- **WA08-dark-harvest:** The guide's third guard, no interruption expected, has no term and is not written.
